doc.title: Harold Mabern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010

title: Living at the Sloan House YMCA on five thousand dollars
summary: He compares 1959 costs to now and explains stretching his savings at the Sloan House YMCA before taking an apartment.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: What was the name of the place?

The Sloan House YMCA. 34th Street between Eighth and Ninth Avenue. Because I had five thousand dollars when I got there. In 1959 five thousand dollars was probably like what, 20 or 30 thousand dollars, because the cost of living was down. I mean Transcontinental Airlines from New York to Chicago by [Inaudible] was 24 dollars and 50 cents. The Four Seasons, the Sheraton, the Waldorf was like 50 dollars a week. You go there now, the occupancy rate is 65 dollars a night. That’s aside from the 300 or 499 dollars, you know. So five thousand dollars was a lot of money. Five thousand dollars is a lot of money now. If somebody just said I’m going to give you five thousand dollars for a piano lesson or a half hour gig, you know. So but I said I’m going to hold on to this money. How can I stretch it? Because we were staying at a hotel in midtown Manhattan called the Flanders. A lot of musicians stayed there. And I think that was something like 10 or 15 dollars a week. But I said I’ve got to make this money — because once this money goes if I don’t preserve it and get some gigs I’m going to be back in Chicago and I had no intention of doing that. So somebody told me about the Y. And I went there and I said okay, I can handle this. Private rooms you know. But you had to go to go to the main bathroom to take a shower. They had a lot of face bowls and stuff, it was big and roomy but you had to pick your time to get your showers in, for your privacy. So then I said but at this point I saved my money and I said I’m going to get an apartment.
